headline: VIDRAFT Releases Fully Open Foundation Model Aether-7B-5Attn: Weights, Code, Data, and Training Logs — All Public
summary: This ~6.59B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model, released under Apache-2.0, includes full training data recipes, code, and logs, enabling complete reproducibility.
details: Korean AI startup VIDRAFT has launched Aether-7B-5Attn, a ~6.59B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts foundation model on Hugging Face. Crucially, it's released under the permissive Apache-2.0 license, making it free for commercial use.

Unlike many "open-source" LLMs that only provide weights, VIDRAFT's release includes the full training data recipes, code, configuration files, training logs, intermediate checkpoints, and evaluation code. This allows for complete reproducibility and verification of the model.

VIDRAFT positions Aether-7B-5Attn as a practical implementation of "Sovereign AI," emphasizing that true AI independence requires the ability to reproduce, verify, and audit the entire model pipeline. This aligns with the philosophy of projects like Allen AI's OLMo.

The model features a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which allows for a larger total parameter count while keeping per-token compute costs efficient. It also incorporates a five-attention hybrid mechanism, combining multiple attention variants for balanced efficiency and context handling.

This reproducibility-first approach sets a higher bar than the industry norm, enabling engineers to independently verify training and audit data provenance. It moves beyond simply running inference or fine-tuning open weights.

The public release is available on the Hugging Face Hub. Developers are encouraged to run their own evaluations using the bundled evaluation code, as specific benchmark scores were not provided in the initial announcement.

headline: China's AI rivals unveil new frontier models challenging US dominance
summary: Chinese AI companies Moonshot and Alibaba have launched new frontier models, Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters) and Qwen3.8 (2.4T parameters), claiming to rival OpenAI and Anthropic's top systems.
details: Moonshot AI and Alibaba have unveiled new frontier AI models, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8, respectively. They claim these models rival the capabilities of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, suggesting a narrowing gap in AI leadership.

Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 is described as the world's largest open-source AI system with 2.8 trillion parameters. Alibaba's Qwen3.8 is a 2.4 trillion parameter model, continuously evolving and also slated for open-weight release.

A key differentiator is their commitment to public availability, contrasting with the proprietary approach of many leading US labs. Moonshot will release full model weights on July 27th, while Alibaba's Qwen3.8 is "going open-weight soon."

While independent testing is still needed to fully assess their capabilities, these releases intensify the US-China technological rivalry. They raise questions about whether the vast US investments in AI can maintain a durable advantage if Chinese rivals can achieve similar performance with fewer resources.

The open-source strategy from China also stands in contrast to Washington's efforts to restrict access to advanced AI technology. This includes export controls on chips and forcing US companies to pull capable systems from the market.
